product: Vertiv sells critical digital infrastructure: power (UPS, switchgear, busway, power distribution, and â€” with the 2026 deals â€” microgrid controls and behind-the-meter/onsite generation orchestration), thermal/cooling (liquid cooling, cold plates, CDUs, chillers, dry coolers, heat rejection), IT infrastructure (racks/integrated modules), plus a growing software and field-services layer (commissioning, fluid management, load testing, lifecycle services). Q2 2026 net sales of $3,274M split $2,647M products / $628M services, with services up ~33% y/y (vs products +22%), so it is still hardware-led but the services annuity is thickening via PurgeRite/Strategic Thermal Labs/ThermoKey/KES.
demand: Demand is growing and Vertiv is selling more, not merely selling differently: Q2 2026 net sales +24% y/y (18% organic, +5% acquisitions, +1% FX), and on July 29, 2026 management raised FY26 guidance across all key metrics to ~$14.0B sales with 30-32% organic growth, guiding Q3 to 34-36% organic and ~24.0-25.0% adjusted operating margin. The growth is AI/high-density-driven and geographically uneven â€” Q2 AMER +29.2% and APAC +28.5%, but EMEA only +1.7% (organic -2.4%), which is the one clearly softening region.
pricing_power: Partially yes, and the evidence is at the margin/cost line rather than in disclosed list-price increases: Q2 2026 adjusted operating margin expanded 410bps y/y to 22.6%, which management explicitly attributes partly to 'favorable price-cost, inclusive of tariff impacts and associated countermeasures'. The counterweight is buyer power â€” Vertiv's own risk factors flag 'less leverage with large customer contract terms', and hyperscaler concentration plus long-dated, multi-phased, fixed-price project contracts limit how much price can be pushed without volume risk.
competition: Vertiv's competitive set spans power (Schneider Electric/APC, Eaton, ABB, Huawei, Delta, Legrand) and thermal (nVent, Munters, Boyd, CoolIT, Motivair/Modine, plus HVAC incumbents Trane and Carrier), with microgrid/behind-the-meter specialists now squarely in scope after the UIG deal. Management is explicit that its 2026 capacity acceleration is intended to 'capture market share', implying Vertiv is currently the net share taker in liquid cooling and integrated thermal-chain solutions while moving onto Eaton/Schneider and grid-interconnect specialists' turf upstream.

market_strategy: Management's stated next-12-months plan is an integration-led roll-up plus capacity expansion: close the ~$1.45B UIG (microgrid/behind-the-meter power) and King Environmental Services (EMEA fluid management) acquisitions in Q4 2026, fold in the earlier-2026 buys (Strategic Thermal Labs, ThermoKey) and 2025's PurgeRite, and spend capex at ~4.0% of revenue (high end of range) to add capacity, funded from a net-cash balance sheet with $5.6B liquidity. The framing is 'grid interconnect to rack' / 'source to chip': extend the portfolio upstream and own more of the stack while staying generation-agnostic and silicon-agnostic, and keep raising guidance as pipelines strengthen.
bull: Q2 2026 net sales +24% y/y (18% organic), and on 2026-07-29 management raised FY26 guidance to ~$14.0B sales / 30-32% organic growth with Q3 guided to 34-36% organic -- AI/high-density-driven demand with dated confirmation (the $2.6B Utility Innovations deal, 09-03).
